title: Diwali Mithai Guide: What to Buy Early, What to Buy Last, How to Store It
excerpt: Dry sweets keep for weeks and milk sweets for days. Shop in that order — preorder kaju katli and soan papdi, buy jalebi on the day, and refrigerate bought milk sweets the day they arrive.
body:
• Diwali falls on Sunday, November 8, 2026, with Dhanteras on Friday, November 6 — buy long-keeping dry sweets first and perishable milk sweets last.
  • Buy kaju katli and soan papdi from a sweet shop and jalebi on the day you serve it; preorder shop sweets the weekend before Diwali, according to TasteOS.
  • Storage follows moisture: besan ladoo keeps 2 to 4 weeks in an airtight tin, kaju katli about a week, and rasgulla and rasmalai only 1 to 3 days in the fridge, according to Desi By Nature.
  • To cut waste, buy perishable milk sweets only in quantities your household can finish within their storage window, and check packing dates, best-before information and FSSAI licence details before paying.

The mithai run fails in two predictable ways: too much is bought too early, and milk sweets sit out until they spoil. Work backwards from how each sweet keeps. Dry, ghee-and-sugar sweets tolerate an early purchase. Milk, khoya and chhena sweets do not, and should be bought close to the day they will be eaten or given.

What to buy, and what to leave to the sweet shop

For a mixed box, start with the long keepers. Desi By Nature groups besan ladoo, atta ladoo, Mysore pak, nankhatai, shakarpara and balushahi among sweets that keep for 2 to 4 weeks at room temperature in airtight tins in a cool, dry place, because low moisture and high ghee and sugar do not support microbial growth. Kaju katli, desiccated coconut ladoo, motichoor ladoo and soan papdi sit in the middle, at about a week.

Some sweets are smarter bought than made. TasteOS advises buying kaju katli because the cashew dough has to hit a precise sugar-syrup stage and turns grainy or sticky if that stage is missed, and buying soan papdi because its dough is pulled and folded repeatedly into fine, flaky strands. Jalebi is different again: it is best within hours of frying, so buy it on the day you serve it. Gulab jamun in syrup keeps for several days in the fridge, according to Desi By Nature, while jalebis soften within hours.

"What to buy, and what to leave to the sweet shop For a mixed box, start with the long keepers."

When to shop

TasteOS puts the practical move a week out: on the weekend before Diwali, call your Indian sweet shop to preorder kaju katli or soan papdi, because sweet shops get very busy in Diwali week. Pick up the dry shop sweets on Thursday, November 5, and leave jalebi until the day it will be served. That sequence is also the waste strategy: nothing perishable sits in the house longer than it needs to.

Before paying, run the checks reported by Janatha Mirror from the festive food-safety drive: choose an established outlet with clean counters, avoid sweets with an unusual smell or discolouration, and on packaged boxes check the packing date, best-before information, ingredients and FSSAI licence details. For loose sweets, ask when they were prepared and how they were stored. The full buyer checklist is in the Janatha Mirror food-safety report.

How to store each type

Keep crisp snacks separate from soft sweets so they do not soften, Desi By Nature advises. Kaju katli can stay airtight at cool room temperature for a few days or be refrigerated for up to about two weeks. Short keepers — khoya barfi, peda, kalakand, milk cake and fresh coconut ladoo — last 2 to 5 days refrigerated and should not sit out on a warm day for more than a couple of hours. The shortest window belongs to rasgulla, rasmalai, sandesh and chhena sweets: 1 to 3 days, refrigerated promptly. Bought milk sweets should go into the fridge the day you receive them. The complete by-type table is in the Desi By Nature storage guide.

Gift boxes and avoiding waste

TasteOS applies the perishable-food rule to dairy sweets in gift boxes: no more than 2 hours at room temperature, or 1 hour if it is above 90°F. Keep boxes containing kalakand or coconut ladoo in the fridge until you walk out the door, and for boxes that will ride around all day, skip the dairy sweets entirely and fill them with besan ladoo, kaju katli and soan papdi, which are fine at room temperature. Rasmalai should not go in a box at all; share it in a lidded container that goes straight into the fridge. Its day-by-day make-ahead and packing plan is at TasteOS.

Throw sweets out on any sour or fermented smell, visible mould, sliminess or discolouration, if milk sweets were left out overnight, or if ghee-rich sweets taste rancid. Buy according to need — perishable sweets only in quantities that can be consumed within their storage period — and the festival ends with an empty box for the right reason.
